Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention
item.description:
Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention

Palestinian journalist Farah Abu Ayyash has returned home to her family following 450 days of detention in Israeli prisons, according to a report by the Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna).

Abu Ayyash, a West Bank correspondent for Iran's Tasnim News Agency, was freed on Thursday night after the Ofer Prison military court ordered her release, dismissing the charges brought against her after she served 15 months under administrative detention.

According to Irna, Abu Ayyash was initially detained on 6 August 2025, during an overnight military raid on her family home in Beit Ummar, north of Hebron. The outlet reported that her arrest was tied to her journalistic work covering local developments across the southern West Bank for Tasnim.

The report further noted that repeated procedural delays prolonged her case, keeping her detained without formal resolution under administrative detention at Damon Prison. Irna also reported that the correspondent was allegedly subjected to torture and mistreatment while in custody.

item.title: Iran warns of 'earth-shattering blow' as Araghchi slams Germany's war stance
item.description:
Iran warns of 'earth-shattering blow' as Araghchi slams Germany's war stance

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi has criticised Germany for supporting Israel-US war on Iran last year and now complaining the conflict has added has added more than 100 billion euros ($112bn) to Europe’s energy costs.

In a post on X, Araghchi said that when Israel-US bombings of Iran began last year, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz  hailed them as "doing Europe's dirty work".

"100bn Euro is nothing compared to the Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people," Araghchi said. 

"Red lines are a thing of the past," he added.

item.title: 'We must be so strong that no dares covet our land', Pezeshkian says
item.description:
'We must be so strong that no dares covet our land', Pezeshkian says

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reminded his countrymen that “we must be so strong that no one dares to covet our land and identity”.

In a post on X marking forthcoming National Youth Day on 8 November, Pezeshkian recalled the "courage of Mohammad Hossein Fahmideh", a 13-year-old Iranian boy killed during the Iran-Iraq war, and paid tribute to children killed in Minab, Lamerd and other parts of the country.

Pezeshkian said: "The names and memories of our children remain in our minds and shape our collective historical memory, so that we know we must be so strong that no one dares to covet our land and identity."

item.title: US denies Iran’s claim that it destroyed US sea drone in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) on Friday denied an Iranian claim that its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had destroyed an unmanned US military surface vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, Anadolu reports. “All U.S. military unmanned surface vessels in the Middle East are accounted for, including a squadron of advanced sea drones on patrol in the Strait of Hormuz supporting CENTCOM’s defensive layer,” CENTCOM said on US social media company X. Earlier Friday, the Iranian Navy said it had destroyed an “enemy unmanned vessel” operating east of the strait, without identifying the vessel or its operator, according to a statement carried by the official IRNA news agency. item.title: Match between Turkish football side Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Beer-Sheva to be played in Georgia
item.description: Turkish football side Besiktas announced on Friday that their UEFA Europa League home match against Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva will be played in the country of Georgia, Anadolu reports. According to a club statement, the 5th round of the Europa League match against the Israeli club will be held on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Batumi Stadium in the coastal city of the same name. The match will be open to Besiktas fans, with further details on ticket sales to be announced at a later date, the Istanbul club said. item.title: UN warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza amid concerns of ‘ethnic cleansing’

item.title: Saudi Arabia suspends travel, entry from Kenya over Ebola concerns
item.description: Saudi Arabia on Friday announced additional precautionary measures against the Ebola virus, including suspending travel to and entry from Kenya, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The measures, introduced following an assessment of the epidemiological situation by health authorities, include suspending travel by Saudi citizens to Kenya and halting the issuance of all types of visas to travelers from the East African country. The kingdom will also prohibit entry to travelers arriving from Kenya, including those traveling through third countries who have stayed in Kenya or other Ebola-affected countries during the 21 days preceding their arrival.
